issues.description: The UML/problem specification declares Ride.abbreviation as type 'char' but the reference solution implements Ride.abbreviation as a String and its constructor/getter use String. At the same time, RollerCoaster and LaunchedRollerCoaster constructors in the solution use 'char' for the abbreviation parameter, creating a mismatch between superclass and subclass signatures. This inconsistency will confuse students about the correct type to use for abbreviation and can lead to compilation errors when implementing constructors that must accept superclass attributes first.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the abbreviation type consistent across specification, template and solution. Preferably follow the UML/problem statement and change the Ride attribute, constructor parameter, and getter to use 'char' (private char abbreviation; public Ride(String name, char abbreviation); public char getAbbreviation()). Also update any subclasses and constructor calls (e.g., RollerCoaster, LaunchedRollerCoaster) to use and forward a char abbreviation. Alternatively, if a String is desired, update the problem statement/UML to specify String for abbreviation and adjust the constructor order in the tasks accordingly.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares the Ride attribute 'abbreviation' as type char (problem_statement.md: '-abbreviation: char'), but the solution's Ride implementation uses a String for 'abbreviation' (Ride.java: private String abbreviation; constructor Ride(String name, String abbreviation) and getter getAbbreviation()). Meanwhile, RollerCoaster and LaunchedRollerCoaster constructors in the solution use a char parameter named 'abbreviation'. This inconsistent representation of the same conceptual attribute ('abbreviation') across the UML/problem statement and the solution (and across solution classes) creates confusion for students about the expected type and constructor signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the 'abbreviation' type across artifacts. Either: (A) change the UML/problem statement to specify 'abbreviation: String' and update any related wording, or (B) change the solution code so Ride uses a char for 'abbreviation' (private char abbreviation), update Ride constructor and getter to use char, and ensure RollerCoaster and subclasses consistently accept and forward char. This removes the ambiguity students must resolve about the expected type.
